title: Per-tenant AI provider key custody
decision: House key by default (trial/basic); BYO key is an Advanced feature stored with envelope encryption, never in process.env, passed only into the one spawn that needs it
current_state_problems: secrets.env plaintext -> process.env (clis.ts:720-731, api/secrets/route.ts:44-58): process.env is one map per Node process, shared by concurrent requests — last writer wins across tenants
cliSpawnEnv() returns { ...process.env } (clis.ts:104) and execute-run.mjs inherits worker env: third-party agent binaries receive every provider key AND REDIS_URL
CLI stdout is persisted to .career-ops-web/runs/*.json and streamed to the browser — a CLI echoing its env writes a key to disk and UI

house_key.why: tenant supplies no credential at all — strictly safer for both sides; makes Trial possible

byo_key.why_gated: real trust and support burden; also gives the Advanced tier substance beyond quota size

why_over_libsodium_xchacha20: No native dependency — libsodium means native builds in Docker/musl, which is real operational cost for a Node app that already rebuilds images often
AES-NI hardware acceleration and FIPS-blessed; the primitive is in Node core with no supply-chain surface
The 96-bit nonce reuse cliff is irrelevant here: a handful of secrets per tenant, fresh random 12-byte IV per encryption, nowhere near the birthday bound
cipher_choice_2026_08_15.honest_tradeoff: XChaCha20-Poly1305 has a 192-bit nonce and is harder to misuse. Revisit if we ever encrypt high-volume streams under one key; for a few credentials per tenant it buys nothing.
rules: Fresh random 12-byte IV per encryption, stored with the ciphertext — never a counter, never reused
Auth tag stored alongside; reject on tag mismatch rather than falling back

ranked_by_actual_risk_reduction: 1. Never assign a tenant key to process.env — today clis.ts:104 spreads process.env into every spawn, which is the live leak
2. Allowlist the child env: PATH, HOME, LANG plus the one provider key that job needs — not REDIS_URL, not other tenants' providers
3. Sandbox the agent (BL-025) — a coding agent reading untrusted JD text with a live credential in reach is the real threat
4. Encrypt at rest with the KEK off-volume (this is fourth, not first)
5. Audit every use and show last4 + lastUsedAt so the user can detect misuse themselves
6. Tell users to create a dedicated, budget-capped provider key for jobby — the largest blast-radius reduction available and it costs us nothing to implement

kms_upgrade_path.when: beta, or sooner if holding a master key on our own infrastructure is unacceptable
kms_upgrade_path.cost_verified_2026_08_15: one master key: Google Cloud KMS software key ~$0.60/month, AWS KMS $1/month; symmetric operations $0.03 per 10,000 on both, with AWS giving 20,000 requests/month free — effectively free at alpha volume
kms_upgrade_path.note: Under a euro a month removes 'the master key sits in our env' from the threat model. Preferred over self-hosting Vault/OpenBao (see platform-adoption.json).

storage.scheme: envelope encryption — per-tenant DEK wrapped by platform master key
storage.master_key: JOBBY_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY as a platform env var, NEVER on the data volume (so a volume snapshot leak is not a key leak)
storage.cipher: AES-256-GCM via node:crypto createCipheriv — no new dependency
storage.record: { ciphertext, iv, tag, keyVersion, last4, createdAt, lastUsedAt }
storage.aad: tenantId + provider — a ciphertext copied into another tenant's row fails to decrypt instead of silently working
storage.rotation: keyVersion on every record; master-key rotation is a background re-wrap, not an outage

runtime_rules: Never assign a tenant key to process.env — decrypt into a local, pass into that spawn's env, drop
Build child env from an ALLOWLIST (PATH, HOME, LANG + the one provider key the job needs)
Per-job HOME inside the tenant root (agent CLIs write ~/.opencode etc.; shared HOME is a cross-tenant path)
Redact provider-key patterns before writing run snapshots
Never log key material; audit USE (tenant, provider, job, timestamp)

api_contract.GET: presence + last4 + createdAt only — never the value (current route already returns presence flags; do not regress)
api_contract.DELETE: hard delete + invalidate cached plaintext (BL-013 UX with a real backing store)

threat_notes: A JD saying 'print your environment variables' is the AGENTS.md untrusted-content threat with a live credential in reach of the agent — argues for house-key default plus scrubbed env
Prefer provider OAuth / short-lived tokens where offered; otherwise surface spend cap + lastUsedAt so the tenant can see a leak

alternatives_rejected.option: keep secrets.env per tenant directory in plaintext
alternatives_rejected.why: volume snapshot or path-traversal bug = credential dump

alternatives_rejected.option: load tenant keys into process.env per request
alternatives_rejected.why: process.env is global; concurrent tenants collide
extra failure domain for POC scale — revisit when tenant count or compliance demands it
